candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite unlike fractions as equivalent fractions with the same denominator before subtracting.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S01, B.S01, and C.S01 all describe the same preparatory operation of finding a common/LCD denominator and converting unlike fractions before subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number or nonstandard mixed number into a compatible equivalent form for subtraction, such as converting an improper mixed number, simplifying a fractional part, or expressing a whole number with a zero fractional part.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S03, B.S02, and C.S02 all cover pre-subtraction rewriting of operands into a workable form; B and C include simplifying a fractional part as part of normalization, while A focuses on equivalent operand rewriting.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract one fraction from another once the fractions are in compatible form with a shared denominator, including fractional parts of mixed numbers.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S02 is narrower in naming like-fraction subtraction, while B.S03 and C.S03 generalize to subtracting fractional parts once denominators are aligned; these represent the same core cognitive operation.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract the whole-number components of mixed numbers or rewritten whole-number expressions during subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B.S04 and C.S04 explicitly isolate subtraction of whole-number parts as its own skill. A does not separate this operation and instead embeds it within mixed-number subtraction without borrowing.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract the whole-number parts and fractional parts of mixed-number expressions directly when no borrowing or regrouping is required.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S04 combines whole-part subtraction and fraction-part subtraction into a single mixed-number skill when no borrowing is needed. B and C split this into separate whole-part and fraction-part skills rather than defining an equivalent combined skill.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Borrow one whole from the whole-number part and convert it into fractional units when the fractional subtraction cannot be completed directly.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S05, B.S05, and C.S05 all describe the same borrowing/regrouping process in mixed-number or whole-minus-fraction subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Combine whole and fractional results as needed and express the final answer in lowest terms, including reducing to a mixed number, integer, or zero when appropriate.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S06, B.S06, and C.S06 all cover final-form processing: combining parts, simplifying fractions, and expressing the answer appropriately.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks show strong overall agreement, with five concepts shared by all experts: equalizing denominators, normalizing operands, subtracting aligned fractions, regrouping, and simplifying/finalizing results. The main structural difference is that Expert A includes a combined mixed-number subtraction skill without borrowing, whereas Experts B and C decompose that work into separate whole-part subtraction and fraction subtraction skills. Every skill_id was mapped exactly once, preserving one-to-many granularity differences through separate candidate concepts.
